## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: secure container runtime, init containers, config-driven rollouts, resource limits, probes, graceful termination, disruption budgets, and network isolation.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext and podSecurityContext for non-root operation
- InitContainer usage and seed data from ConfigMap
- Rolling restart triggers via checksum/config annotation
- Probes and termination settings
- PodDisruptionBudget and NetworkPolicy integration

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch skeleton (conceptual)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: worker
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/config: "<computed-from-configmap>"
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: myorg/worker:latest
          securityContext:
            runAsUser: 1000
            runAsGroup: 1000
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]
          env: []
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "256Mi"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
      initContainers:
        - name: seed-data
          image: busybox
          command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /config/bootstrap/* /data/" ]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: worker-data-pvc
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: worker-config
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests your ability to design an isolated audit pattern with in-cluster API access, RBAC scoping, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control
- In-cluster API access using Secrets and ConfigMaps
- PVC-backed persistent logs and InitContainers for tooling
- NetworkPolicy for egress control to restrict traffic to the collector
- Health checks (readiness/liveness probes) for reliability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-baseline
  namespace: example
data:
  baseline.json: |
    {"pods": [], "services": []}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-auth
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: " collector-auth-token"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:
        - name: COLLECTOR_URL
          value: "http://collector.audit-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives for practical automation: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and PVCs, plus robust scheduling and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and jobTemplate usage
- ConfigMap and Secret as environment sources
- PVC mounting in Jobs for persistent backups
- Concurrency policy and job history controls
- Rollback and validation workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: dataops
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 7
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: postgres-backup
            image: postgres:15
            env:
            - name: BACKUP_DIR
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: BACKUP_DIR
            - name: DB_HOST
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: DB_HOST
            - name: DB_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_USER
            - name: DB_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_PASSWORD
            command:
            - /bin/bash
            - -c
            - |
              DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)
              BACKUP_FILE="/backups/${DB_NAME}-${DATE}.sql"
              pg_dump -h $DB_HOST -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME > $BACKUP_FILE
            volumeMounts:
            - name: backup-storage
              mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
          - name: backup-storage
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Validation Plan
1. Check CronJob creation: `kubectl get cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Verify schedule: `kubectl describe cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
3. Test manual job: `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/db-backup test-backup -n dataops`
4. Monitor job completion: `kubectl get jobs -n dataops -w`
5. Validate backup files: `kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n dataops -- ls -la /backups`

## Rollback Plan
1. Delete CronJob: `kubectl delete cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Clean up test jobs: `kubectl delete jobs -l job-name=db-backup -n dataops`
3. Remove backup files if needed: Access PVC and delete specific backup files
4. Recreate with corrected manifest if issues persist

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests comprehensive CKAD skills including per-namespace isolation, configuration management with ConfigMaps and Secrets, InitContainers for dependency setup, sidecar patterns for auxiliary services, health probes for reliability, RBAC for security, and NetworkPolicy for traffic control.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers for runtime dependency installation
- ConfigMaps and Secrets for configuration and credential management
- Sidecar containers for TLS certificate rotation
- Readiness and liveness probes for health monitoring
- Namespace isolation and NetworkPolicy for security boundaries
- Dead-letter queue implementation on PVC storage
- At-least-once delivery semantics with batch processing

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ns-collector
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: install-deps
    image: alpine:latest
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache nats-cli']
  containers:
  - name: collector
    image: collector:latest
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef:
        name: ns-collector-config
    - secretRef:
        name: ns-collector-creds
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
    volumeMounts:
    - name: dlq-pvc
      mountPath: /dlq
  - name: tls-sidecar
    image: tls-sidecar:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls-certs
      mountPath: /etc/tls
  volumes:
  - name: dlq-pvc
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: dlq-pvc
  - name: tls-certs
    secret:
      secretName: tls-certs
```

## Trade-offs
- **At-least-once vs exactly-once**: At-least-once provides simpler implementation but may cause duplicate processing
- **Sidecar overhead**: TLS rotation adds resource consumption but improves security
- **PVC vs temporary storage**: PVC provides persistence but increases complexity and cost
- **NetworkPolicy restrictions**: Improve security but may impact debugging and monitoring capabilities

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your understanding of namespace-scoped automation, PVC usage, and secure scanning workflows within Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace CronJob with PVC mounts for manifests and logs
- Lightweight containerized scanner (e.g., trivy-lite)
- ConfigMap-based findings storage
- InitContainer for tool provisioning (jq, curl)
- Readiness and liveness probes on Job Pods
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress restrictions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: manifest-scan
  namespace: example-ns
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: tools-installer
            image: busybox:1.36
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              wget -q https://github.com/stedolan/jq/releases/download/jq-1.6/jq-linux64 -O /tmp/jq
              chmod +x /tmp/jq
              apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tmp
          containers:
          - name: scanner
            image: trivy-lite:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: manifests
              mountPath: /manifests
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              export PATH=/tmp:$PATH
              for manifest in /manifests/*.yaml; do
                trivy scan --format json -o /logs/$(basename $manifest).json $manifest
              done
              kubectl get configmap security-scan -n example-ns -o yaml > /logs/configmap-backup.yaml
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - ls
                - /logs
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - cat
                - /tmp/health
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: manifests
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: manifest-pvc
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: log-pvc
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs ConfigMap**: Using a PVC for logs allows for larger log volumes and retention, but requires storage provisioning. ConfigMaps are simpler but size-limited.
- **InitContainer vs Sidecar**: InitContainers run once per pod startup; sidecars run continuously. For a CronJob, InitContainers are more cost-effective.
- **NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress improves security but may break updates if registries change. Consider using DNS whitelisting rather than specific IP ranges.
- **Probe timing**: Aggressive probes may cause premature failures; conservative settings increase job execution time.
- **CronJob frequency**: More frequent scans catch vulnerabilities faster but increase cluster load and API calls.
